body.statement: Determine a closed numerical expression for \(r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\), with no unknown-law optimization, for which \[c_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\le R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\le C_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\] holds uniformly over all \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\). As the required supervised endpoint reduction, prove \[r_\epsilon(n,0,d)\asymp_\epsilon\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\},\] the matched rate recorded in \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap}\), without treating that endpoint as a new result. For the benchmark experiment \(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{known}}_{n,d,\epsilon}\), prove the exact fixed-parameter limit \[\lim_{m\to\infty}R_\epsilon(n,m,d)=R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)\qquad\text{for every fixed }n\ge1\text{ and }d\ge2.\] Along every sequence \(n\to\infty\), give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions written only as elementary limits or inequalities in \(n\), \(m_n\), and \(d_n\), with no shorthand through \(r_\epsilon\), for each of \(R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)\to0\), \(R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)=O(n^{-1})\), and the strict order improvement \(R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)=o\{R_\epsilon(n,0,d_n)\}\).
body.justification: The matched all-regime rate is the theorem-level kernel: it makes the number of treatment-only records a quantitative information parameter and must certify an order-changing, not merely monotone, value of annotation.
body.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 and the catalogued \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap}\) result resolve the supervised obstruction, while ChengAnanthakrishnanCai2021, ChakraborttyDai2024, and Kato2025 provide regular semi-supervised efficiency statements. The requested result strictly refines the supervised boundary into a two-sample frontier by recovering it at \(m=0\), proving the fixed-\((n,d)\) limit to the explicitly defined known-\(P_{XA}\) experiment, and characterizing exactly when auxiliary records change the minimax order.
body.consumer: Sections 2.1 and 4 of ChengAnanthakrishnanCai2021 gain a baseline-only decision rule for comparing another chart-reviewed outcome with another treatment--covariate record when working nuisance models are not trusted.
